questions.question: Corpus luteum of pregnancy is maintained by______
questions.explanation:
Human chorionic gonadotrophin (HCG) causes persistence of the corpus luteum and prevents menstruation in pregnancy.

The fate of the corpus luteum

• If the ovum is not fertilized, about 2 days before the end of the monthly cycle, the corpus luteum in the ovary involutes

• If fertilization occurs, under the influence of human chorionic gonadotropin, the corpus luteum in the mother’s ovary grows to about twice its initial size by a month or so after pregnancy begins

• The corpus luteum secretes estrogens and progesterone and maintains the decidual nature of the uterine endometrium, which is necessary for the early development of the fetus

• The corpus luteum of pregnancy involutes slowly after the 13th to 17th week of gestation. After that time, the placenta secretes sufficient quantities of progesterone and estrogens to maintain pregnancy for the remainder of the gestation period

questions.question: FSH receptor is present in_____
questions.explanation:
• Granulosa cells express the FSH receptor.

• Theca interna cells express LH receptor.

Theca interna cells have many LH receptors. LH acts via cAMP to increase conversion of cholesterol to androstenedione. The theca interna cells supply androstenedione to the granulosa cells. The granulosa cells make estradiol when provided with androgens.

Granulosa cells have many FSH receptors. FSH facilitates their secretion of estradiol by acting via cAMP to increase their aromatase activity. Mature granulosa cells also acquire LH receptors, and LH also stimulates estradiol production.

questions.question: A 30-year-old lady is using the basal body temperature method for contraception. She takes note of a rise in her body temperature for abstinence during the fertile period. The increase in basal body temperature in the mid-luteal phase is due to which of the following hormones?
questions.explanation:
An increase in basal body temperature in the mid-luteal phase is due to the effect of progesterone on the hypothalamic thermoregulatory centre.

Immediately after ovulation, corpus luteum is formed, which secretes progesterone in preparation of the body for potential pregnancy during that cycle. This progesterone acts on the hypothalamus and increases basal body temperature. Charting the daily basal body temperature will show an increase of approximately 0.5 to 1 degrees fahrenheit shortly after ovulation.

Since the rise in basal body temperature coincides with ovulation, abstaining from sexual intercourse until at least 3 days after the woman’s temperature has risen above her regular temperature significantly lowers the chance of pregnancy. Alternatively, using barrier methods (e.g. condom, diaphragm) during this time will prevent pregnancy.

However several factors (e.g fever, sleep deprivation etc.) that change the basal body temperature, can affect the efficacy and reliability of this method.

questions.question: A blood sample is drawn on day 20 of the menstrual cycle of a young woman undergoing evaluation for irregular menstruation. Serum level of which of the following hormones help in assessing whether her cycle was ovulatory or not?
questions.explanation:
Whether her cycle was ovulatory or not can be validly assessed by the reported serum level of progesterone.

Day 20 usually corresponds to the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle. In case of anovulatory cycles, no corpus luteum will be formed and so progesterone levels will be low. Hence progesterone levels are valuable to predict if the cycles were ovulatory or not.

questions.question: Secretion of estrogen is maximum ______
questions.explanation:
• Estro­gen comes from the ovary, and two peaks of secretion occur one just before ovulation and one during the mid-luteal phase.

• After menopause, estrogen secretion declines to low levels.

questions.question: Which of the following hormones inhibit FSH and LH secretion in the luteal phase?
questions.explanation:
Estrogen inhibits FSH and LH secretion in the luteal phase.

Feedback regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis

Luteal phase: the corpus luteum secretes large quantities of progesterone and estrogen. They exert a negative feedback effect on the anterior pituitary gland causing the suppression of both FSH and LH secretion.

Preovulatory period: The high level of estrogens at this time (or the beginning of progesterone secretion by the follicles) causes a positive feedback stimulatory effect on the anterior pituitary leading to a surge of LH and to a lesser extent, FSH.

Follicular phase: secretion of estrogen, progesterone from the corpus luteum decreases which leads to loss of negative feedback effect of these hormones on the anterior pituitary. Therefore, pituitary secretion of FSH begins to increase again, as much as twofold. LH secretion increases slightly as well.

GnRH stimulates FSH and LH secretion. Growth hormone and IGF may cause an increase in FSH and LH levels.

questions.question: Which of the following statement can be regarded as primary action of inhibin?
questions.answer: D. It inhibits secretion of FSH
questions.explanation: The inhibins inhibit FSH secretion by the gonadotrophs of the anterior pituitary (hence the name inhibin) in a classic negative feedback arrangement.

questions.question: Inhibin B is secreted by______
questions.explanation:
The inhibins are produced by the granulosa cells of the ovarian follicle, as well as other tissues, including the pituitary, the brain, the adrenal gland, the kidney, the bone marrow, the corpus luteum, and the placenta. Inhibin A is produced by the corpus luteum whereas inhibin B is mainly produced by granulosa cells of the follicle

FSH specifically stimulates the granulosa cells to produce inhibins.

Just before ovulation, after the granulosa cells acquire LH receptors, LH also stimulates the production of inhibin by granulosa cells.

questions.question: Source of progesterone during normal menstrual cycle______
questions.explanation:
The source of progesterone during the normal menstrual cycle is corpus luteum.

Progesterone is also secreted by the placenta, and the ovarian fol­licle (in small amounts).

questions.question: Which of the following is the source of estrogen?
questions.explanation: Estrogen are secreted primarily by the granulosa cells of the ovarian follicles, the corpus luteum, and the placenta .

questions.question: Regarding the two-cell—two-gonadotropin hypothesis which of the following is true?
options: FSH and LH inhibits the release of estrogen and progesterone
FSH acts on granulosa cells and LH on theca cells
FSH stimulates estrogen while LH inhibits estrogen
FSH feedback inhibits hypothalamus while LH feedback inhibits pituitary
questions.answer: B. FSH acts on granulosa cells and LH on theca cells
questions.explanation:
The two-cell—two-gonadotropin hypothesis:

• Estradiol synthesis requires the contribution of two distinct cell types:

• The theca and granulosa cells within the follicle and

• The theca-lutein and granulosa lutein cells within the corpus luteum

• The follicular theca cells, under the control of LH, produce androgens that diffuse to the follicular granulosa cells, where they are converted to estrogens via an FSH-supported aromatization reaction. The granulosa cells cannot convert progesterone to androstenedione because of the lack of the enzyme 17α-hydroxylase.

questions.question: Regarding the action of progesterone which of the following is true?
options: Increases sensitivity of uterus to oxytocin
Causes marked proliferative changes in uterus
questions.explanation:
Progesterone inhibits LH secretion.

Actions of progesterone

• Has negative feedback effects on FSH and LH secretion during the luteal phase.

• Maintains secretory activity of the uterus during the luteal phase.

• Maintains pregnancy.

• Raises the uterine threshold to contractile stimuli during pregnancy, i.e decreases sensitivity of the uterus to oxytocin.

• Participates in the development of the breasts.

• Increases body temperature

• It stimulates respiration, and the alveolar PCO2 in women during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle is lower than that in men.

• Large doses of progesterone produce natriuresis, probably by blocking the action of aldosterone on the kidney.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most potent type of estrogen found in women of reproductive age group?
questions.explanation:
• Estradiol is the most abundant in the reproductive age group and is 12 and 80 times more potent than estrone and estriol respectively.

• The principal sex steroids in females are estrogen, progestin, and androgen. Three estrogens are present in significant quantities—estradiol, estrone, and estriol.

questions.question: Which is the predominant estrogen in the plasma of premenopausal non-pregnant women?
questions.explanation:
Estradiol is the predominant estrogen in the plasma of premenopausal non-pregnant women. It is primarily secreted from ovaries.

Estrone is synthesized from dehydroepiandrosterone in adipose tissue stroma. Estrone is the abundant circulating form of estrogen in postmenopausal women.

In pregnancy, the placenta uses dehydroepiandrosterone and its 16 alpha hydroxyl derivative to form large amounts of estrone and estriol.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about estrogen action?
options: Development of secondary sexual characters in female
questions.explanation:
Estrogen does not stimulate osteoclast. Rather it prevents osteoporosis by inhibiting osteoclastic activity.

Actions of Estrogen

• Causes maturation and maintenance of the fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, and vagina.

• Causes proliferation and development of ovarian granulosa cells.

• Proliferation of endometrium

• Causes the development of female secondary sex characteristics at puberty.

• Maintains pregnancy.

• Lowers the uterine threshold to contractile stimuli during pregnancy.

• Causes the ductal development of the breasts.

• Has both negative and positive feedback effects on FSH and LH secretion.

• Up-regulates estrogen, LH, and progesterone receptors.

• Increases secretion of angiotensinogen and thyroid binding globulin

• Epiphyseal closure of long bones

• Increase libido by acting on the hypothalamus.

• Salt and water retention before menstruation

• ↓LDL cholesterol

• ↑ the local production of NO→vasodilation

• Inhibit osteoclast, prevent osteoporosis

questions.question: A 12-year-old girl is undergoing pubertal changes. Her tanner stage is stage 4 for breast development and pubic hair scale. Which of the following pubertal changes is not due to estrogen?
questions.answer: B. Pubic and axillary hair growth
questions.explanation:
Pubarche or development of axillary and pubic hair is not due to estrogen. It is due to testosterone (in both the sexes).

Puberty in females :

• Involves the beginning of menstrual cycles (menarche), breast development (thelarche), and an increase in adrenal androgen secretion (adrenarche).

• Estradiol induces the development of secondary sex characteristics, including the breasts and reproductive tract, and increased fat in the hips.

• Estrogens also regulate the growth spurt at puberty, vaginal cornification and cervical mucus production, induce closure of the epiphyses, have a positive effect in maintaining bone formation, and can antagonize the degrading actions of parathyroid hormone on bone.

questions.question: β HCG is secreted by which of the following organs?
questions.explanation:
β HCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) is secreted by the syncytiotrophoblast of the placenta.

Some important features of β HCG:

• hCG is a glycoprotein that contains galactose and hexos­amine.

• It is produced by the syncytiotrophoblast of the placenta.

• It is made up of α and β subunits.

• hCG-α is identical to the α subunit of LH, FSH, and TSH.

• hCG is primarily luteinizing and luteotropic and has little FSH activity.

• Its presence in early pregnancy in urine is the basis of the various laboratory tests for pregnancy, and it can sometimes be detected in the urine as early as 14 days after conception.

questions.question: Progesterone has how many carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Progesterone has 21 carbon atoms.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about milk ejection?
options: The neuroendocrine part of anterior pituitary is involved.
Its secretion occurs by contraction of lactiferous sinus.
questions.answer: A. The neuroendocrine part of anterior pituitary is involved.
questions.explanation:
The neuroendocrine part of the anterior pituitary is not involved in milk ejection. The posterior pituitary is involved in milk ejection reflex.

The posterior pituitary secretes oxytocin, which is responsible for milk ejection. The anterior pituitary produces prolactin, which is responsible for lactogenesis.

Figure: Milk Ejection Reflex

questions.question: Which of the following hormones is responsible for milk ejection?
questions.explanation:
• Oxytocin causes contraction of the myoepithelial cells lining the mammary ducts and ejects milk during suckling. But, it has no galactogenic effect.

• Prolactin is responsible for milk secretion.

• Estrogens are primarily responsible for the proliferation of the mammary ducts and the progesterone for the development of lobules.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a function of oxytocin?
questions.explanation: Lactogenesis is not a function of oxytocin. It is caused by prolactin.

questions.question: The maximum contractile force of any muscle per square cm cross-sectional area is _____
questions.explanation:
The strength of a muscle is determined mainly by its size, with a maximal contractile force between 3 and 4 kg/cm2 of muscle cross-sectional area.

• The female muscle can achieve almost exactly the same maximal force of contraction as that of the male muscle per square centimeter of cross-sectional area.

• Most of the difference in total muscle performance between males and females lies in the extra percentage of the male body that is muscle, which is caused partly by endocrine differences:

• Testosterone secreted by the male testes has a powerful anabolic effect in causing greatly increased deposition of protein in the muscles.

• Estrogen increases the deposition of fat in the female, especially in the breasts, hips, and subcutaneous tissue.

questions.question: A budding athlete who is keen to participate in long races visits his dietician for a discussion on his exercise capacity. When an athlete runs at a speed typical for the marathon race, the time until complete exhaustion is maximal with which of the following diets?
questions.explanation:
When athletes run at speeds typical for the marathon race, the time that they can sustain the race until complete exhaustion (also known as endurance) is maximal with a high-carbohydrate diet.

A person, who consumes a high-carbohydrate diet, stores far more glycogen in muscles than does a person who consumes either a mixed diet or a high-fat diet. Therefore, endurance is enhanced by a high-carbohydrate diet.

When athletes run at speeds typical for the marathon race, their endurance is approximately the following:

Diet
Minutes

High-carbohydrate diet

240

 Mixed diet
120

 High-fat diet
85

questions.question: A professional athlete uses phosphocreatine to improve his sprinting capacity and maximize muscle power during a 100 m dash race. Which of the following energy systems is utilized by the muscles of the athlete's body during a dash race?
questions.explanation:
The phosphagen system is utilized by the muscles of the athlete's body during a dash race.

The combined amounts of cell ATP and cell phosphocreatine are called the phosphagen energy system. These substances together can provide maximal muscle power for 8 to 10 seconds, almost enough for the 100-meter run. Thus, the energy from the phosphagen system is used for maximal short bursts of muscle power.

Energy systems:

• The phosphocreatine-creatine system: The combined amounts of cell ATP and cell phosphocreatine are called the phosphagen energy system. These substances together can provide maximal muscle power for 8 to 10 seconds.

• The glycogen–lactic acid system: can provide 1.3 to 1.6 minutes of maximal muscle activity.

• The aerobic system: The aerobic system is the oxidation of foodstuffs in the mitochondria to provide energy. It can sustain mucle activity for an unlimited time (as long as nutrients last).

questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding muscles adapted for endurance running?
options: Twice as large in diameter compared to fast twitch fibers
questions.answer: D. Twice as large in diameter compared to fast twitch fibers
questions.explanation:
Slow-twitch fibres, which are adapted for endurance running, are not larger in diameter than fast-twitch fibres. Fast-twitch fibres are about twice as large in diameter compared with slow-twitch fibres.

Fast-Twitch and Slow-Twitch Muscle Fibers

• Fast-twitch fibres can deliver extreme amounts of power from a few seconds to a minute.

• The enzymes that promote rapid release of energy from the phosphagen and glycogen–lactic acid energy systems are more active in fast-twitch fibres.

• Fast-twitch fibres are about twice as large in diameter compared with slow-twitch fibres.

• Gastrocnemius muscle has a higher preponderance of fast-twitch fibres, which gives it the capability of forceful and rapid contraction of the type used in jumping.

• Slow-twitch fibres are mainly organized for endurance, especially for the generation of aerobic energy.

• They have far more mitochondria than do the fast-twitch fibres.

• They contain considerably more myoglobin. The extra myoglobin increases the rate of diffusion of oxygen throughout the fibre.

• The enzymes of the aerobic metabolic system are considerably more active in slow-twitch fibres.

• The number of capillaries is greater in the vicinity of slow-twitch fibres.

• Soleus muscle has a higher preponderance of slow-twitch muscle fibres and therefore is used to a greater extent for prolonged lower leg muscle activity.

questions.question: Regarding respiratory adjustment seen during exercise, which of the following statements is true?
options: Activity of joint proprioceptors is important factor in increasing ventilation
Arterio-venous difference in oxygen concentration remains constant
questions.answer: A. Activity of joint proprioceptors is important factor in increasing ventilation
questions.explanation:
Signals from joint proprioceptors play a role in stimulating the respiratory drive during exercise.

Regulation of respiration in exercise

• During strenuous exercise, O2 consumption and CO2 for­ mation can increase as much as 20- fold. Yet in the healthy athlete, the arterial PO2, PCO2, and pH remain almost exactly normal. This is because the alveolar ventilation increases along with the increased level of oxygen metabolism.

• Part of this stimulation of alveolar ventilation results from direct stimulation of the respiratory center by nervous signals. An additional part is believed to result from sensory signals transmitted into the respiratory center from the contracting muscles and joint proprioceptors.

• During strenuous exercise, the utilization of O2 in the entire body can increase to 75% to 85%. So, essentially all the oxygen is given to the exercising muscles leading to an increased arterio-venous difference in oxygen concentration.

questions.question: Exercise at high altitudes is not hindered by which of the following factors?
options: Fall in the total oxygen supply available
questions.answer: A. Fall in blood bicarbonate levels
questions.explanation:
The fall in blood bicarbonate levels is compensatory, and it helps increase the exercise effort, not hinder it.

Adaptation at High Altitudes

The work capacity is reduced at high altitudes and this reduction is in direct proportion to the decrease in O2 uptake. (Option B)

Immediate exposure to low PO2 at higher altitudes stimulates the arterial chemoreceptors, and this stimulation increases alveolar ventilation.

This immediate increase in pulmonary ventilation upon rising to a high altitude blows off large quantities of CO2, reducing the PCO2 and increasing the pH of the body fluids (Respiratory alkalosis). This raised pH inhibits the brain stem respiratory center and opposes the increased ventilation. So, respiratory alkalosis will hinder the maximal exercise effort. (Option C).

To compensate for this respiratory alkalosis, kidneys reduce hydrogen ion secretion and increase bicarbonate excretion. This reduces plasma and cerebrospinal fluid bicarbonate concentration and brings the pH towards normal. This removes the inhibitory effect of alkalosis on respiration. Hence the fall in blood bicarbonate facilitates the exercise effort.

NOTE

Lactic acid causes extreme fatigue. (Option D)

Ordinarily, the pyruvic acid from glycolysis enters the mitochondria of muscle cells and reacts with oxygen to form many ATP molecules.

However, when there is insufficient oxygen (at high altitudes), most of the pyruvic acid then is converted into lactic acid, which diffuses out of the muscle cells into the interstitial fluid and blood.

questions.question: A 30-year-old man who is extremely motivated to participate in high-intensity exercises is advised to quit smoking by this physician. Which of the following is not a reason behind smoking-related decrease in exercise capacity?
options: Increased fluid secretion into the bronchial tree
Paralysis of cilia on the surfaces of the respiratory epithelial cells
questions.explanation:
Smoking causes no change to the sensitivity of the chemoreceptors.

Effect of Smoking on Pulmonary Ventilation in Exercise

• Nicotine causes constriction of the terminal bronchioles of the lungs, which increases the resistance of air flow into and out of the lungs.

• The irritating effects of the smoke causes increased fluid secretion into the bronchial tree and some degree of swelling of the epithelial linings, which again increases airflow resistance.

• Nicotine paralyzes the cilia on the surfaces of the respiratory epithelial cells. As a result, much debris accumulates in the passageways, and this adds further to the difficulty in breathing.

• All these factors together make even a light smoker experience respiratory strain during maximal exercise, and their level of performance may be reduced.

• In persons with severe emphysema, as much as four-fifths of the respiratory membrane can be destroyed; then, even the slightest exercise can cause respiratory distress. Chronic smoking is an important cause of emphysema.

questions.question: Which of the following is seen in response to exercise?
options: Increased cerebral blood flow due to increase in systolic blood pressure
Increased blood flow in muscles after at least 15 minutes of activity
questions.explanation:
Exercise causes an increase in body temperature.

Almost all the energy released by the body’s metabolism of nutrients is eventually converted into body heat. Since metabolism rises significantly during exercise there is an increase in the body temperature. This increase in body temperature is significant and even lethal conditions such as heatstroke can easily develop in an athlete.

Other options:

Option A: Cerebral blood flow is “autoregulated” extremely well between arterial pressure limits of 60 and 140 mm Hg. That is, the mean arterial pressure can be increased to as high as 140 mm Hg without significant change in cerebral blood flow.

Option B: The arterial Po2, Pco2, and pH remain almost exactly normal even though during strenuous exercise, O2 consumption and CO2 for­mation can increase as much as 20­ fold.

Option C: The increase in blood flow to exercising muscles is immediate and not after 15 minutes.

questions.question: Which of the following circulatory systems demonstrates an increase in blood supply during exercise?
questions.explanation:
Coronary circulation increases during exercise.

During exercise, blood flow

• Decreases in inactive skeletal muscles, kidney, liver, and GIT

• Remains unaltered in brain (due to autoregulation)

• Increases in exercising muscles, coronary circulation

• Initially decreases due to redistribution, but later increases due to an increase in temperature in the skin

questions.question: Which of the following is not true regarding exercise-induced physiological changes?
options: Left shift of Hb-O2 dissociation curve
Increase in blood supply to muscle
questions.answer: A. Left shift of Hb-O2 dissociation curve
questions.explanation:
Left shift of Hb-O2 dissociation curve is not seen during exercise.

During exercise, several factors shift the Hb-O2 dissociation curve considerably to the right, thus delivering extra amounts of O2 to the active, exercising muscle fibers.

The right shift of Hb-O2 dissociation curve is due to the following:

• Release of large quantities of CO2 by the exercising muscles

• Increase in the hydrogen ion concentration in the muscle capillary blood

• Increase in the temperature of the muscle by 2° to 3°C

questions.question: Which of the following is the main cause of increased blood flow to exercising muscles ?
options: Increased sympathetic discharge to peripheral vessels
questions.answer: B. Vasodilatation due to local metabolites
questions.explanation:
The tremendous increase in muscle blood flow that occurs during skeletal muscle activity is caused mainly by chemicals acting directly on the muscle arterioles to cause dilation.

These chemicals include:

• Potassium ions,

• Adenosine triphosphate (ATP),

• Lactic acid, and

• Carbon dioxide.

Other factors leading to increased muscle flow include

• sympathetic nervous system activation

• increase in arterial pressure, and

• increase in cardiac output.

However, the effect of local metabolites is greater than these factors in increasing the muscle blood flow. Hence, the best answer is local metabolites.

questions.question: Isometric (static) exercise differs from isotonic (dynamic) exercise in that it causes a greater increase in _______.
questions.explanation:
There is a sharp rise in the diastolic blood pressure in isometric exercise. This is due to the sustained compression of the blood vessels by the contracting muscles. In isotonic exercise, there is much vasodilatation in exercising muscles. So, even though the muscles are contracting, there is no rise in the diastolic blood pressure.

Option (a) Since the muscle pump is more active during isotonic exercise, the venous return is higher in isotonic exercise.

Option (b) The increase in the muscle blood flow is less compared to isotonic exercise since inflow of blood is obstructed by sustained compression exerted by the contracting muscle.

Option (d) Isometric exercise increases the after load of the heart leading to less increase in the stroke volume of the heart.

questions.question: Regarding circulatory adjustments made during exercise, ________.
options: The cardiac output increases more than ten-fold.
Increase in cardiac output is mainly due to an increase in stroke volume.
The mean systemic filling pressure rises at the onset of heavy exercise.
In severe exercise, the systolic blood pressure falls.
questions.answer: C. The mean systemic filling pressure rises at the onset of heavy exercise.
questions.explanation:
The mean systemic filling pressure rises tremendously at the onset of heavy exercise.

This occurs as a result of

• The sympathetic stimulation contracts the veins.

• Tensing of the abdominal and other skeletal muscles of the body compresses many of the internal vessels, thus providing more compression of the entire vascular system and causing a still greater increase in mean systemic filling pressure.

Cardiovascular Changes in Exercise

• The maximum increase of cardiac output is 4-fold that can commonly be achieved by the untrained runner and 7-fold that can be achieved in some marathon runners.

• The increase in heart rate accounts for a greater proportion of the increase in cardiac output than the increase in stroke volume during sustained strenuous exercise.

• Exercise also causes an increased venous return due to

• Increased activity of the respiratory pump

• Increased activity of the muscular pump

• Increased venous tone due to sympathetic stimulation

• Increased blood flow from arteries to veins

• In severe exercise, there is increased systolic and mean blood pressure due to

• vasoconstriction of the arterioles and small arteries in most tissues of the body

• increased pumping activity by the heart

• a great increase in mean systemic filling pressure caused mainly by venous contraction.

• As seen in the figure, point A is the resting cardiac output. On exercise, there is a rise in the mean systemic filling pressure shown on the X-axis.

• The venous return also rises which causes the cardiac output to reach point B, which is 4 times the normal resting cardiac output.

questions.question: Which of the following is not true regarding the increase in the blood supply of muscles during exercise?
questions.explanation:
During exercise, there is increased beta-adrenergic stimulation.

Medullae of the two adrenal glands secrete large amounts of norepinephrine plus epinephrine into the circulating blood during strenuous exercise. The epinephrine often has a slight vasodilator effect because it excites more of the beta-adrenergic receptors of the vessels, which are vasodilator receptors, in contrast to the alpha vasoconstrictor receptors excited especially by norepinephrine.
